hints: Look closely at how many hydrogen bonds (dashed lines) join each pair, and whether each labelled base has one ring or two rings.
Remember A pairs with T using 2 hydrogen bonds, while G pairs with C using 3 hydrogen bonds, and only thymine has a methyl ($H_3C$) group on a single ring.
walkthrough:
**Count the hydrogen bonds between the pairs**

Start with the dashed lines in the middle. The top pair (C to D) has 2 hydrogen bonds. The bottom pair (A to B) has 3 hydrogen bonds.

Remember the rule:
$$A-T = 2 \text{ hydrogen bonds, } G-C = 3 \text{ hydrogen bonds}$$

**Sort purines from pyrimidines**

Double rings are purines (adenine and guanine). Single rings are pyrimidines (thymine and cytosine). So C and A are purines, while D and B are pyrimidines.

**Spot the thymine clue**

Look at D at the top right. It is a single ring (pyrimidine), it pairs with 2 hydrogen bonds, and it has a distinctive $H_3C$ methyl group on top. That combination is unique to thymine in DNA. So label D is correct.

options.A: Label A is a double-ring purine forming 3 hydrogen bonds, which identifies it as guanine, not adenine.
options.B: Label B is a single-ring pyrimidine forming 3 hydrogen bonds, which identifies it as cytosine, not guanine.
options.C: Label C is a double-ring purine forming 2 hydrogen bonds, which identifies it as adenine, not cytosine.
options.D: Label D is a single-ring pyrimidine with a methyl group forming 2 hydrogen bonds with adenine, which is exactly thymine.
